title: A Cover for the Extraction
premise: Freya Almeida, a disgraced intelligence analyst fired from three agencies for seeing patterns no one wanted to see, receives a call on a burner phone that shouldn't exist — from her dead mentor, Elias Voss, who faked his death and is now embedded in a private syndicate planning an 'accidental' infrastructure collapse in Lisbon. Voss needs someone outside the system, someone deniable, and Freya's paranoia makes her the perfect asset. As she infiltrates the operation under a forged identity, she discovers Voss isn't a whistleblower but a true believer, and that the attack is a cover for a power grab inside the agencies that ruined her. In the end Freya must choose between exposing the truth — which will destroy what's left of her old life and the man she's come to love inside the syndicate — or letting the attack proceed to protect him; she stops the collapse, burns her cover forever, and walks away with nothing but the truth and a new name.
about_author: Petra Villalobos is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade advising governments on infrastructure vulnerabilities before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the people systems discard, drawing on a life spent between Lisbon, Miami, and too many airport lounges.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Living off savings in a rented room in Porto, Freya maintains her polished lie of retirement while cataloguing the habits of a woman waiting to run. A routine errand turns wrong when she spots surveillance tradecraft aimed at her. The emotional beat: dread sharpening into alertness — the past has found her address.

chapters.title: A Voice That Should Be Ashes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The burner phone rings: Elias Voss, her mentor, officially killed in a car bomb two years ago. He offers proof he's alive and a warning — something catastrophic is scheduled in Lisbon, dressed as an accident. Emotional beat: grief curdling into fury and hunger; the only man who ever believed her is asking for help.

chapters.title: Three Agencies' Worth of Enemies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Tomás Ribeiro, a domestic security officer investigating anomalies in Lisbon's grid contracts. He flags Freya's old case files, not knowing she's already in the city. Emotional beat: two hunters circling the same blind spot, each convinced the other is the threat.

chapters.title: Cover Story: Marta Ferreira
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Using forged credentials, Freya enters Meridian Logistics, the syndicate front, as a compliance auditor. She meets Daniel Okafor, the charming operations lead whose kindness feels dangerously real. Emotional beat: the intoxicating relief of being competent again — and the first crack of guilt over deceiving Daniel.

chapters.title: The Schedule of Accidents
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Deep in Meridian's files, Freya reconstructs the plan: a staged transformer failure during a summit week, engineered to kill power, markets, and reputations simultaneously. Voss goes dark when she pushes for details. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the pattern she was fired for seeing is real, and it's bigger than one attack.

chapters.title: What Voss Buried
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, flashback-tinged. His recruitment into the syndicate, his genuine belief that burning the old order is mercy, and his manipulation of Freya as the perfect deniable instrument. Emotional beat: tragic self-justification — a good man's ideals rotting into ownership of other people's lives.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Daniel corners her with evidence she isn't Marta Ferreira — then reveals he's been feeding doubts about Meridian to outsiders himself. They become reluctant allies, then lovers, both lying about their deepest loyalties. Emotional beat: tenderness under mutual suspicion; love arriving precisely where betrayal should.

chapters.title: Tomás Closes In
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. He traces the burner phone network to Freya and confronts her hours before the attack window opens. Instead of arresting her, he listens — because his own agency's fingerprints are on the grid contracts. Emotional beat: a bitter alliance born of shared institutional betrayal.

chapters.title: Lisbon, Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs converging. Freya and Daniel race to trigger the failsafe while Voss, exposed, tries to accelerate the collapse; Tomás buys them time by misdirecting his own command chain. Freya faces Voss in the substation control room and must talk him down or end him. Emotional beat: everything at stake compressed into minutes — duty, love, and identity colliding.

chapters.title: A New Name at Dawn
chapters.summary: Resolution, Freya's POV. The attack is stopped, Voss is dead by his own hand rather than capture, and the scandal guts three agencies — including the last remnants of Freya's old life. Daniel chooses exile with her; Tomás buries the file that would have destroyed them both. Emotional beat: hard-won peace — she keeps nothing she built before, and finally wants nothing she can't carry.
